homemaker._doc: Stay at home: no offers, small daily household bonus, autonomy likes chores / cooking / groceries more.

seeking._doc: Only somebody looking for work takes an offer on their own: searching in the last search_days days, or the household has less than broke_below coins, or (no_computer_looks) the household has no computer to search from; never within min_days_between_changes of the last hire / quit.

first_job._doc: Who gets offered what (task 19j): a first job or a new offer is a weighted pick over the careers the person qualifies for, so children do not all become baristas. weight = base + skill x skill_w + trait bonus x trait_w + aspiration match + the job board (openings, hot demand), then divided down for each housemate already in that career. teen_careers are the ones with a part-time level 1 (teens only, level 1).

skip._doc: When something else of the player's queued at shift time counts as 'chose to skip' (task 19j): a decision per person, day and kind, not an automatic skip. chance = base_<kind> x trait_mult x mood_mult (max), and a housemate who already skipped today makes it almost impossible (housemate_mult) unless a skipping trait AND a bad mood give a strong reason. The 'skip work today' command is not touched.

switch._doc: A young adult may change careers (with friction): only in the first young_days of adulthood, only in the first max_level levels, never within min_days_in_job of being hired or min_days_between_changes of the last change. The daily chance rises when the job fits badly (performance under unhappy_below) and the new career must fit clearly better (better_by x). They start the new career at level 1 with start_performance_penalty less performance, and lose the old level.
